content.text: productive cough for ≥3mo/y for 2+ consecutive years
enlargement of airspaces distal to the terminal bronchioles
accompanied by destruction of the airspace walls
*classically seen in smokers, usually affects the upper lobes

: begins with chronic airway inflammation that progresses to emphysema, a condition characterized by irreversible bronchial narrowing & alveolar hyperinflation ⇢ loss of diffusion area leads to V/Q mismatch w/ resultant hypoxemia & hypercapnia
▪︎⇣ DLCO: establishes presence of emphysema (normal in chronic bronchitis)
(e.g., enlarged lungs, flattened diaphragm, ⇡ AP diameter)
PaO2 ≤55mmHg is an indication for continuous supplemental O2
➁ Assessment of airflow limitation (% of predicted FEV1 ⇢ GOLD)
➂ Symptoms/exacerbation history (mMRC dyspnea scale, CAT score)
*ICS should only be used in combo w/ LABA/LAMA
▪︎mortality benefit directly proportional to # of hours O2 is
▪︎acute worsening of respiratory symptoms necessitating additional therapy

: advanced age, productive cough, longer duration of COPD, history of ABX therapy, COPD hospitalization within past year, chronic mucous hypersecretion, eosinophil count >340cells/µL, ⊕comorbidities (e.g., IHD, HF, DM)
: exclude pneumonia, PTX, pulmonary edema, pleural effusion
▪︎HFNC O2 therapy, NIPPV, intubation & mechanical ventilation
